newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Three bids for Dutch fixed-line phone licences.
newsitem.headline: Three bids for Dutch fixed-line phone licences.

text.p: Three groups have submitted applications for licences to build and operate national fixed-line public telephone networks in the Netherlands, the Dutch government said on Tuesday.
The following three groups confirmed separately that they had submitted applications: British Telecom Plc and Netherlands Railways (NS); Global One; andEnertel.
Global One is a joint venture of Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom.
Enertel is a consortium of Dutch regional power companies and local cable television network operators.
The government plans to award one or two licences, announcing its decision before the end of this year.
A licence will enable the holder to compete in fixed-line telephony with Dutch PTT (Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV) which at present operates the only conventional Dutch national phone network.
The government plans full liberalisation of the Dutch telecommunications market by January 1, 1998.
